name: Gijs Bartholomeus
intro: I study mathematics at the intersection of topology, biology, and medicine.
about: I am a DPhil student in Mathematics at the University of Oxford and a member of Balliol College. My interests lie in topological data analysis, algebraic topology, and mathematical biology, with a particular curiosity about the connections between mathematics and medicine.

My route into mathematics began in medicine. Alongside my medical training, I studied mathematics and physics at Utrecht University, completing master's degrees in all three subjects. That background continues to shape the questions I find interesting: how can mathematical structure help us understand complex biological systems?
My supervisors include Helen Byrne, Alain Goriely, Lida Kanari, and Heather Harrington. Previously, I worked with Ard Louis at Oxford on simplicity bias and sloppiness in gene regulatory networks.

interests.title: Topological data analysis

interests.title: Algebraic topology

interests.title: Mathematical biology
interests.text: Using mathematical models to understand the dynamics and organisation of living systems.

interests.title: Mathematics & medicine
interests.text: Bringing a clinical perspective to questions in mathematical modelling and the analysis of biomedical data.
